overall: The AG found the Framingham School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to respond to a minutes request within 10 days, but not intentionally, and found no violation on the timely-release and executive-session review complaints.

allegations.summary: Complainant requested the Sept. 5 open and executive session minutes on Sept. 6 and alleged the committee failed to timely respond to that request.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee failed to do so, we find that it violated the Open Meeting Law by not properly responding to a request for minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the failure to respond to the minutes request was an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to find that this violation was intentional.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to timely release the open session minutes from the Sept. 5 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee reviewed and approved the September 5 minutes on October 3, its second meeting thereafter, and thus complied with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to review the Sept. 5 executive session minutes at its next meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by reviewing the September 5 executive session minutes at its October 3 meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements (respond to minutes requests within 10 days).
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
